text: {"headline":"High 99215 share concentrated on low-complexity patients points toward upcoding, but the documentation sample is too thin to confirm or refute it.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The complexity breakdown is the strongest signal. This provider's 99215 share exceeds the all-provider share in every complexity band, including patients with zero or one chronic condition, who account for most of the 99215s. Several sampled 99215s on those patients carry only routine diagnoses: upper respiratory infection (C0030577, C0032075), follow-up encounters (C0030705, C0032365) and rash (C0031020, C0032580). That pattern is consistent with upcoding rather than a sicker panel, although the sampled high-complexity 99215s (e.g., C0032106, C0032164) look appropriate. The records review cannot settle the question: only 4 documented 99215s came back, so the absence of unsupported claims is too thin to judge, and 3 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line are weak evidence of templated or inflated notes. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed, prioritizing the URI, rash and Z09 follow-up visits, and check whether the documented MDM and time reflect the actual encounter."}
